title: Spring warmth had positive links to between-taxon moth date variance in two English samples in 1993-2015
abstract: We split equal-taxon moth catch-date variance into within-taxon spread and between-taxon mean-date separation. We used 117 consecutive trap-year pairs in England and Scotland in 1993-2003 and 2004-2015. Spring warmth slopes for between-taxon variance were +79.24 and +81.18 days squared per C in England. Their eight-test intervals were +0.33 to +158.15 and +48.03 to +114.33. Scottish intervals included zero. All four main within-taxon intervals included zero. Matched calendar dates retained the English results. The early English result weakened with stricter coverage. Nonoverlapping-pair fits were imprecise. Seasonal truncation, weather-dependent capture, selected taxa, coarse weather and few years limit inference. This is a catch association, not a causal climate effect or evidence of harm. Code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and regeneration instructions are included. External records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Spring warmth slopes for two parts of equal-taxon catch-date variance. Bars use eight-test t intervals. Brown marks show weak residual support. These are selected catch associations.

citations.reason: Adapt sampling builder and retrieval code. Raw biological records overlap. We add a date-variance decomposition and new outcome tests.
